subtitle: linear realizations of {1ᵃ, (y−k)ᵇ, yᶜ}
summary: Every multiset {1ᵃ, (y−k)ᵇ, yᶜ} with 1 ≤ k < y/2 and a ≥ y has a linear realization: a Hamiltonian path in Kᵥ with exactly those edge lengths.
problem: For all integers y, k, a, b, c with 1 ≤ k < y/2, a ≥ y and b, c ≥ 0, the multiset {1ᵃ, (y−k)ᵇ, yᶜ} has a linear realization.

That means the vertices {0, 1, …, v−1} of the complete graph Kᵥ, where v = a + b + c + 1, can be arranged into a Hamiltonian path whose edge lengths |pᵢ₊₁ − pᵢ| are exactly a copies of 1, b copies of y − k and c copies of y.
statement: 1 ≤ k < y/2,  a ≥ y,  b, c ≥ 0   ⟹   {1ᵃ, (y−k)ᵇ, yᶜ} has a linear realization
title: Agırseven–Ollis conjecture
